neighbours.label: the verb at the point where a sentence turns to whether an action has an effect ('would make a difference', 'would matter'), as against 'make' with an ordinary object
fire: Many people doubt that recycling one bottle will make a difference to the planet.
She wondered whether her small donation would make any difference at all.
Even a few extra minutes of exercise each day can make a real difference.
Some students feel that one more hour of study won't make a difference.
He was not sure his letter to the senator would make a difference.
Volunteers hope their weekend clean-up will make a lasting difference.
Critics argue that the new tax will hardly make a difference to emissions.
If everyone turned off one light, it would make a big difference.
quiet: Many people like to make bread at home on the weekend.
She wondered whether to make pasta or soup for dinner.
Even a few extra minutes in the oven can burn the cake.
Some students like to make flash cards before the exam.
He was not sure how to make a paper boat for his son.
Volunteers will make sandwiches for the visitors on Saturday.
Critics argue that the new tax is unfair to small farmers.
If everyone brought one dish, the party would have plenty of food.

predictions: fire 0.4-0.85 on ' make' when the context asks whether an act has an effect; 'make a cake / make dinner' and similar sentences without the effect frame below 0.15
